title: I Followed the Theme-Park Lightning Policy Out of the Skip-the-Line They Sold

parts.text: I scanned a paid skip-the-line at 2:18 p.m. and the attendant sent everyone to the regular queue because of lightning they said was nearby. The app still sold skips. The sky was bright. I was twenty-nine, holding two plastic coins I had bought at 2:11. Policy on the map said pauses refund or extend. They offered a sticker. I photographed the radar, the receipt, and the sticker. Then I asked guest services, not the attendant, for the pause clause. At 2:27 thunder happened somewhere, and they kept selling skips on a screen I could see.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: They are still selling skips while the pause clause is in guest services' hand.

social.video_title: Lightning pause, still selling skip coins — Part 1/2
social.description: Bright sky, 2:11 purchase, a sticker. Guest services had a clause. Would you have taken the sticker?

parts.text: Guest services extended the coins and voided the sticker as currency. We rode at 3:40 when the pause lifted. The attendant learned the radar. I did not clap at the sky. Paid lines are a product. Lightning is weather. Stickers are not refunds. The plastic coins worked once, which is all they promised if you read the map. I read maps. I still got wet later, honestly, but not in the wallet.

social.description: Extended coins, 3:40 ride, radar literacy. Was nearby a sales pitch?
